title: Search Plan
description: A deterministic research plan produced from a 'ready' ResearchRequest (see research_request.schema.json). This describes HOW a future research step should look for information — it does not perform any search, and none of its fields may be read as a claim that a source exists or that a query has produced results. See docs/search-strategy.md.
$comment: search_scope reuses the same value/source/basis/raw_value envelope as ResearchRequest.constraints, carried through unchanged, so explicit-vs-inferred provenance survives from the request into the plan. Every other top-level field (search_queries, source_types, preferred_source_characteristics, pagination_strategy, verification_strategy) is a strategy decision made by the planner itself, not a request constraint — keeping those two kinds of information in separate fields is what preserves the distinction docs/search-strategy.md requires.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the plan conforms to. Optional; assumed current if omitted.

research_request_id.description: Content fingerprint (sha256 of the canonical ResearchRequest JSON) identifying which request this plan was built from. ResearchRequest (research_request.schema.json) has no id field of its own, so this is computed rather than copied — the same request content always yields the same id.

search_queries.description: Generated query variations. Deliberately plural where the request supports it — different phrasings surface different sources. A rationale accompanies each so the strategy is auditable, not a black box.

query.description: The query text itself. A phrase to search for — not a claim it has been searched.

source_types.description: Categories of source to look for, ordered most-preferred-first for the objective of building a structured dataset.

preferred_source_characteristics.description: Qualities a good source for this plan should have (e.g. structured over narrative). Describes what to look for, not any specific source found.

search_scope.description: The subset of the originating ResearchRequest's constraints that bound this search, carried through with their original explicit/inferred provenance intact. A key present here means that dimension is bounded; an absent key means unbounded on that dimension (not unknown).

season.description: Canonical season, same format as the result schema.

date_from.description: Inclusive lower bound on event date.

date_to.description: Inclusive upper bound on event date.

expected_result_count.description: An ESTIMATE only, computed from documented competition-structure knowledge when available (e.g. Premier League = 38 matches per club per season since 1995-96). Omitted entirely when no such rule applies — never guessed. Not a claim that any source or query has actually returned this many results; no search has been performed.

basis.description: The documented rule/reasoning behind the estimate.

pagination_strategy.description: How a future research step should think about paging through a source. A heuristic starting point, not a claim about any real source's actual structure — no source has been visited yet.

approach.description: 'bounded_range_lookup': scope is bounded by a season or explicit date range. 'iterative_unbounded_lookup': no such bound exists (e.g. an all-time head-to-head), so more pages may be needed.

max_pages_per_source.description: Suggested soft cap; a heuristic default, not a measured fact about any source.

requires_second_source.description: Whether an independent second source is required before a record can be marked verified. Derived directly from the request's 'verification' constraint.

fields_to_cross_check.description: Which result_record fields must be cross-checked across sources when requires_second_source is true.

on_disagreement.description: Policy for when cross-checked sources disagree. The planner's current deterministic default is 'prefer_official_source_else_mark_conflicting'; the other values remain valid schema options for future use.
